messages:
maya: Heads-up — we
re seeing several customer tickets reporting sudden 429 cascades and unexpected token billing after the new rate-policy canary went live (20% traffic) last night. Details in thread.

maya: Symptom summary: streaming sessions start, then a burst of 429s on subsequent chunk requests. Clients retry aggressively, which amplifies token consumption. Noticed clustering around 03:10-03:16 UTC for first report.

maya: Example repro the customer provided (trimmed):
```
POST /v1/chat/stream
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-13b",
  "stream": true,
  "history": "...long convo..."
}
```
Customer saw first chunks arrive, then 429s on socket reads and client libs retried, causing additional generate calls.

sam: I pulled the rollout dashboard. Canary policy was rl-2026-staggered, pushed at 2026-03-16T02:50 UTC to 20% of sessions. The canary reduces burst_tokens and lowers per-second steady RPS. Canary cohort shows p95 latency slightly improved but retry_count per-key jumped ~3x. Token-burn spikes correlate with retry spikes.

oliver: Root cause hypothesis: the change lowered burst_tokens (40 -> 20) but kept Retry-After behavior unchanged. Many client SDKs do immediate or linear retries without jitter; compressing retries into the smaller burst window causes repeated 429s and subsequent retries, producing a feedback loop.

julie: Affected customers (hosted): acme-inc, beta-sms, shoply. Dedicated customers not in canary per logs; no dedicated pool alerts.

maya: Quick SRE repro checklist:
1) `SELECT count(1) FROM request_events WHERE api_key = '<key>' AND code = 429 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16T03:00' AND '2026-03-16T03:30'`
2) `rictl policy get rl-2026-staggered --format yaml` to inspect rules
3) `rictl canary status --policy rl-2026-staggered` to confirm cohort membership

sam: Current policy excerpt we pushed: 
```
policy_id: rl-2026-staggered
rules:
  - per_key: true
    window_seconds: 60
    burst_tokens: 20   # previously 40
    steady_rps: 2
    retry_after_header: true
```

oliver: Mitigation options:
- Fast rollback of canary (remove cohort)
- Hotpatch policy in canary to raise burst_tokens closer to previous (e.g., 35)
- Gate retries at ingress for canary cohort (limit retries per-minute per-key)
- Update client-facing guidance to recommend exponential backoff + jitter and include Retry-After semantics

sam: Hotfix plan I can run now: patch canary policy to bump burst_tokens -> 35, add a short-lived gateway retry cap (3 retries/min per key) for canary cohort, and enable a billing burn anomaly alert (token-burn > 20% baseline over 10m). Commands:
```
rictl policy patch rl-2026-staggered --set rules[0].burst_tokens=35
rictl rollout apply --policy rl-2026-staggered --cohort canary
ingressctl set retry-cap --cohort rl-2026-staggered-canary --limit 3 --window 60
monitorctl create alert --name "per-key-token-burn" --query "token_burn_pct > 20" --window 10m
```
Propagation note: policy patches hit edge gatekeepers in ~45s-2m; caches may take up to 5m.

julie: If we rollback the canary instead, what's the exact rollback command and expected exposure time?

sam: Rollback command: `rictl rollout remove --policy rl-2026-staggered --cohort canary` (or set percentage to 0). That will stop assigning new sessions to canary and should be visible in dashboards within ~1-3m; existing sessions may still be bound until they reconnect.

oliver: My recommendation: do the patch (increase burst_tokens) as the fastest protective move, plus ingress retry cap to limit billing feedback loops. If symptoms persist after 10m, remove the canary.

maya: Customer comms: will notify impacted customers that we
applied a mitigation (bumped canary burst and added retry cap) and advise client library updates (exp backoff + jitter, honor Retry-After). Drafting msg and will DM for PR.

deploy-bot: deployment started: policy/rl-2026-staggered patch -> burst_tokens=35 (canary), ingress retry-cap applied
deploy-bot: deployment completed: 52s

sam: Post-deploy signals: canary cohort retry-rate down ~65%, 429 rates trending back toward baseline, token-burn per-key falling. One affected customer reports billing delta returning to expected levels after ~9 minutes.

julie: Support will pause outbound escalations until we confirm stability for another 30m. Maya, share the customer note when ready.

maya: Draft sent in DM. Closing thread unless new alerts pop. :thumbsup:
